senses.gloss: To give up an activity, a plan, or a belief before it is finished or fulfilled.
senses.ru: отказываться от, отказаться от; бросать, забросить (дело)
examples: They *abandoned* the search when it got dark.
The city has *abandoned* plans for a new stadium.
He refused to *abandon* hope of finding her.

senses.gloss: To take in information and understand it.
examples: It takes time to *absorb* so much new material.
She *absorbed* everything the coach told her.
I was still *absorbing* the news when the phone rang.

senses.gloss: To take in force, shock, or a cost so that it does less damage.
examples: Good running shoes *absorb* the shock of each step.
The company *absorbed* the extra cost instead of raising prices.
The foam panels are *absorbing* most of the noise from the street.

senses.gloss: To play music that supports a singer or another musician.
examples: A pianist will *accompany* the choir.
She sang while her brother *accompanied* her on guitar.
He has *accompanied* some of the best singers in the country.

senses.gloss: To happen or exist at the same time as something else.
examples: A high fever usually *accompanies* the flu.
Thunder *accompanied* the heavy rain all afternoon.
The article was *accompanied* by three photographs.

senses.gloss: To tell someone that you have received what they sent.
examples: Please *acknowledge* receipt of this email.
They never *acknowledged* my application.
The office has *acknowledged* our letter but has not answered it.

senses.gloss: To do something in order to deal with a situation, especially quickly.
examples: We have to *act* before the deadline.
The doctor *acted* quickly and saved him.
By *acting* fast, the crew kept the fire from spreading.

senses.gloss: To behave in a particular way.
examples: He *acts* strangely around his boss.
She *acted* as if nothing had happened.
Stop *acting* like a child.

senses.gloss: To change the way you behave so that you can live or work well in a new situation.
examples: Children *adapt* quickly to a new school.
He *adapted* well to life in the city.
The team is still *adapting* to the new rules.

senses.gloss: To change a thing slightly so that it can be used for a new purpose.
examples: You can *adapt* the recipe for a smaller pan.
They *adapted* the garage into a workshop.
The bathroom has been *adapted* for wheelchair users.

senses.gloss: To put two or more numbers together to get a total.
examples: If you *add* 15 and 27, you get 42.
She *added* the three columns twice to be sure.
He checked the bill, *adding* the figures in his head.

senses.gloss: To put something with something else to make it bigger, better, or complete.
examples: *Add* a little salt to the sauce.
They *added* a second bathroom last year.
We are *adding* two more chairs to the table.

senses.gloss: To give attention to a problem and try to deal with it.
examples: The mayor promised to *address* the housing shortage.
Your letter *addressed* none of my questions.
The report has *addressed* every complaint on the list.

senses.gloss: To write on a letter or package the name and place it is being sent to.
examples: *Address* the envelope to the head office.
The package was *addressed* to my old apartment.
She spent the morning *addressing* holiday cards.

senses.gloss: To get used to a new situation or a new place.
examples: It takes a few weeks to *adjust* to the night shift.
He *adjusted* to college life faster than we expected.
My eyes were still *adjusting* to the dark.

senses.gloss: To give someone a medicine or a medical treatment.
examples: A nurse will *administer* the shot.
They *administered* first aid at the scene.
The vaccine is being *administered* at all county clinics.

senses.gloss: To manage an organization, a fund, or a program and be responsible for it.
examples: A local bank *administers* the trust.
She *administered* the estate after her father died.
The program has been *administered* by the state for ten years.

senses.gloss: To allow someone to enter a place, a school, or a hospital.
senses.ru: впускать, впустить; принимать, принять (в больницу, в вуз)
examples: This ticket *admits* two people.
The college *admitted* only a tenth of its applicants.
She was *admitted* to the hospital overnight.

senses.gloss: To give someone money before the time it is normally due.
examples: Can you *advance* me fifty dollars until Friday?
The company *advanced* him a month's pay.
The bank has *advanced* the money for the repairs.

senses.gloss: To tell someone a piece of information formally or officially.
examples: Please *advise* us of any change of address.
We were *advised* that the flight had been canceled.
The clerk is *advising* passengers of the delay.

senses.gloss: To state firmly and publicly that something is true.
examples: She *affirms* that she was at home all evening.
Both sides *affirmed* their commitment to the deal.
The governor has *affirmed* her support for the plan.

senses.gloss: To tell people that they matter and that their feelings are valid.
examples: Good teachers *affirm* their students.
The letter *affirmed* everything she had been feeling.
She felt *affirmed* by the group's warm response.

senses.gloss: To keep food or drink for a long time so that its flavor develops.
examples: They *age* the cheddar for two years.
The whiskey was *aged* in oak barrels.
The beef has been *aging* in a cooler for a month.

senses.gloss: To plan or intend to do something.
examples: We *aim* to finish the roof before it rains.
The program *aimed* to get teenagers reading again.
The new law is *aiming* to cut traffic deaths in half.

senses.gloss: To bring people, plans, or ideas into agreement.
examples: We need to *align* the budget with our goals.
Several senators *aligned* themselves with the governor.
The two departments are finally *aligned* on the schedule.

senses.gloss: To present a television or radio news program.
examples: She *anchors* the evening news.
He *anchored* the network's election coverage for twenty years.
They have been *anchoring* the morning show together since March.

senses.gloss: To be attractive or interesting to someone.
examples: The idea of a long drive doesn't *appeal* to me.
The show *appealed* mostly to younger viewers.
The simpler design is clearly *appealing* to first-time buyers.

senses.gloss: To make an urgent public request for help or information.
senses.ru: обращаться с призывом, взывать; просить (о помощи)
examples: Aid groups *appeal* for donations every winter.
Police *appealed* for witnesses to come forward.
The family is *appealing* for information about their son.

senses.gloss: To perform or take part in a film, a show, or a public event.
examples: She has *appeared* in more than thirty movies.
The band *appeared* on a late-night talk show.
He is *appearing* at a small club downtown next week.

senses.gloss: To express strong approval of a decision or an action.
examples: I *applaud* their decision to reopen the library.
Critics *applauded* the change in policy.
The move has been widely *applauded* by teachers.

senses.gloss: To spread or put a substance onto a surface.
examples: *Apply* sunscreen every two hours.
She *applied* a second coat of paint.
The nurse is *applying* a bandage to his arm.

senses.gloss: To be relevant to a particular person or situation.
examples: The discount *applies* to members only.
That rule *applied* only to last year's students.
These instructions don't *apply* to your model.

senses.gloss: To rise in value over time.
examples: Homes in this area *appreciate* about four percent a year.
His shares *appreciated* while he was overseas.
The painting has *appreciated* sharply since 2010.

senses.gloss: To set a weapon or an alarm system so that it is ready to go off.
senses.ru: ставить на боевой взвод; ставить на сигнализацию, включать (охрану)
examples: *Arm* the alarm before you leave the house.
She *armed* the security system and locked the door.
The device had already been *armed* when the squad arrived.

senses.gloss: To put things in a particular order or position.
examples: *Arrange* the chairs in a circle.
She *arranged* the flowers in a tall vase.
The books are *arranged* by author.

senses.gloss: To rewrite a piece of music for particular voices or instruments.
examples: He *arranged* the song for full orchestra.
The carol has been *arranged* for four voices.
She is *arranging* the score for a smaller band.

senses.gloss: To rise to a higher rank or a more powerful position.
senses.ru: восходить, взойти (на престол); подниматься (по служебной лестнице)
examples: Few managers *ascend* that quickly.
He *ascended* the throne at nineteen.
No woman had ever *ascended* to the court before her.
